title: Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality
abstract: arXiv:2610.13123v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A solid understanding of the predictive success of deep neural networks (DNNs) remains elusive. For example, while many data-dependent metrics exist that seek to predict model quality of DNNs, these metrics may be expensive to compute for large datasets and/or may be impossible to compute when training datasets are not released. A practical and effective predictor of model quality involves analyzing DNN weight matrices, as prior work has established that heavy-tailed spectral distributions in trained weight matrices can be strongly predictive of model quality. However, such metrics lack a rigorous statistical justification. In this work, we aim to understand why these metrics perform well, from a statistical perspective. To do so, we employ a probabilistic framework to derive the marginal likelihood for a DNN, evaluated using only the final layer weights. translated_title: 为什么重尾权重谱能够预测模型质量
translated_abstract: 对深度神经网络（DNN）预测成功的坚实理解仍然难以捉摸。例如，虽然存在许多试图预测DNN模型质量的数据相关指标，但这些指标在大型数据集上的计算成本可能很高，和/或在训练数据集未公开时可能根本无法计算。一个实用且有效的模型质量预测方法涉及分析DNN权重矩阵，因为先前的工作已经证明，训练后权重矩阵中的重尾谱分布能够对模型质量产生很强的预测能力。然而，这类指标缺乏严格的统计学论证。在这项工作中，我们旨在从统计学角度理解这些指标为何表现良好。为此，我们采用概率框架来推导DNN的边际似然，且仅使用最后一层权重进行评估。在大型卷积DNN和大型语言模型（LLM）上，我们发现这种边际似然（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文通过概率框架推导出仅基于DNN最后一层权重的边际似然，首次从统计学角度解释了为什么训练权重矩阵中的重尾谱分布能够有效预测模型质量。
en_tdlr: This paper employs a probabilistic framework to derive the marginal likelihood of DNNs using only final layer weights, providing a rigorous statistical justification for why heavy-tailed weight spectra strongly predict model quality.
